description: Two three-input NOR gates and a single inverter, the three sections independent of one another.

inputs.text: One of the three inputs into the gate whose output is J: that output is 10V only while every one of them is low.
One of the three inputs into the gate whose output is K: that output is 10V only while every one of them is low.
The input to the inverter, which has nothing to do with the two NOR gates; with nothing patched here it counts as low.

outputs.text: 10V while A, B and C are all low, 0V as soon as any of them goes high.
10V while D, E and F are all low, 0V as soon as any of them goes high.
The inverse of G: 10V while G is low, 0V while G is high.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
